batchName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284) - Latin words
chapterName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What was the title Augusta that Julia Domna carried?
questions.explanation: She handled much of Caracalla’s official correspondence.

questions.question: Caracalla gave civitas to every free person in the empire. What is civitas?
questions.explanation: Why he did it is still unclear.
questions.sourceQuote: he granted Roman citizenship (*civitas*) to every free person in the empire.

questions.question: What was a donativum, which every new emperor needed?
options: A cash bonus for the troops
questions.explanation: Paying it pushed emperors to mix ever more bronze and copper into the coins.
questions.sourceQuote: each needing a quick bonus (*donativum*) for the troops

questions.question: Who were the coloni of the late empire?
options: Tenant farmers bound to the soil
questions.explanation: They were an early model for medieval serfdom.
questions.sourceQuote: becoming tenant farmers bound to the soil (*coloni*)

questions.question: Elagabalus married a virgo Vestalis. Who was she?
options: A Vestal Virgin, a priestess sworn to chastity
A priestess of the sun god
questions.sourceQuote: he married a Vestal Virgin (*virgo Vestalis*), a priestess sworn to chastity.

questions.question: Macrinus was praefectus praetorio. What was that?
questions.explanation: He was behind Caracalla’s murder in 217.

questions.question: Later rulers called themselves domini instead of princeps. What does domini mean?
questions.explanation: The change showed open monarchy replacing the old pretence.

questions.question: Zenobia was probably paraded in Aurelian’s triumphus. What was it?
questions.explanation: Later writers said she retired to a villa at Tibur.
questions.sourceQuote: his triumph (*triumphus*), the victory parade through Rome
